title: builder-refuse treats the mutation test files as test paths, so a builder cannot write mutants
why: Coordinator 16:45 CST Nov 8. Incident: #2310's builder wrote six mutants into hooks/mutate_guard.py, and builder-refuse let it through. On main 2ac382cc6, AUTHOR_MUTATION_TESTS in hooks/guard.py (mutate_guard.py, mutate_shared.py, janitor/mutate_sweep.py) is read only by the test-author scope check. Its comment says "A builder keeps editing them: they are not test paths". That contradicts owner item 437 a (12:16 CST Nov 8: builders never write test content). Records that argue the carve-out, to rewrite in place: decision agents-get-standing-rules (its builder scope line says to add mutants to hooks/mutate_guard.py when the brief asks); decision red-run-trailer-on-test-commits ("Mutation tests are not test paths, so they need no trailer"); the hooks/guard.py comment at AUTHOR_MUTATION_TESTS. Overlap: step notes-fix-builder-mutants (#1675, ready) built the coordinator's pick c of 17:55 CST Nov 7, "builders may add mutants", in its version of decision builders-cannot-edit-tests; owner item 437 a supersedes that pick. Step tier-boundaries-enforced (#1904) carries decision builders-cannot-edit-tests too. Fix shape: builder-refuse treats the three files as test paths. Red case: a builder Edit that adds a mutant to hooks/mutate_guard.py is refused.
